name: Orca ADE
description: Orca ADE server: run Claude Code, Codex and more in parallel worktrees

upstream.$note: Upstream ships desktop packages only (AppImage/deb/rpm/dmg/exe), no server image. Its documented headless path is `orca serve` from the extracted AppImage (docs/reference/headless-linux-server.md), which is what the image wraps.

positioning.$note: The bare slug /deploy/orca is held by Paul Zarudnev's template (0 deploys, created 2026-09-15). It builds a Dockerfile from GitHub on every deploy (slow first boot) and ships no agent CLIs, only node+npm. Ours is a prebuilt GHCR image with Claude Code, Codex, gh, git, build-essential, ripgrep preinstalled, and a documented browser-only pairing flow.

policy.$note: tosscreen CLEAR. Who receives unrequested traffic? Nobody: the server only accepts clients holding its pairing credential (device token + E2EE key). Anonymous visitors to the domain get a 'paste a pairing URL' screen. Outbound traffic is whatever the deployer's own agents do in their own repos, with their own subscriptions.

topology.$note: Single service, single volume at /data. Orca's state (device registry, E2EE key, projects, settings) lives under HOME=/data/home, so pairing and cloned repos survive redeploys. Verified: fresh deploy -> new container hostname, same paired browser reconnects, project still there.

orca.build: Dockerfile in this repo, built + smoke-tested + pushed by .github/workflows/image.yml (amd64 only; Railway is amd64)
orca.startCommandNote: Deliberately unset. Railway execs a start command raw and discards ENTRYPOINT; the image relies on tini (PID 1, reaps agent/PTY children) and orca-boot (chowns the root-owned volume, drops to the non-root orca user via setpriv, derives the pairing address).
orca.healthcheckNote: orca serve's HTTP listener serves the bundled web client; / maps to web-index.html with 200, no auth needed. Boot to ready is ~20s.

PORT.$note: Pinned so Railway's injected PORT and the domain target port agree. orca-boot passes it as --port.

ORCA_PAIRING_ADDRESS.$note: Empty -> orca-boot advertises https://$RAILWAY_PUBLIC_DOMAIN, which Orca normalizes to wss:// with implicit 443 (Railway's edge). Without --pairing-address Orca advertises ws://127.0.0.1:<port> and remote clients cannot connect. Set only for a custom domain.

findings: Orca binds 0.0.0.0 (IPv4) and has no bind flag in serve mode; Railway's public edge and healthchecker reach it fine. Private-network (IPv6) access would not work, but nothing needs it.
Without gh the UI shows a 'GitHub CLI is not installed' banner and loses PR/issue/check views; gh is in the image.

The pairing credential prints on every boot in deploy logs as 'Web client URL' and 'Pairing URL'. Observed: after a claimed URL, the next boot mints a new device token, but already-paired clients keep working across restarts.
Upstream's noisy dbus errors and an opencode-binder 'SQLite database does not exist' stack trace appear on every boot; both are harmless.

regeneration.$note: orca-source was deleted 2026-09-25. repair.py writes the full config straight to template 8229a738 via templateUpsertConfig and is the regeneration master, same as relay_template.py for orca-ade-w-relay.
